summary: Frontend-only regression for the new pairing share-card feature. All required testIDs present on the pairing detail screen, share-card-button visible at bottom and tappable, tapping it on web shows the expected app-toast ('Image sharing works on the mobile app — open Pairly in Expo Go') and the button does NOT get stuck in 'Creating card…' state. Off-screen PairingShareCard is correctly positioned off-screen (x=-9983, y=-482) — no visible bleed, no scroll padding added. No red-box or console errors from react-native-view-shot, expo-sharing, or the PairingShareCard render. Regression smoke passed: login (chef@pairly.app) → open recent pairing → detail loads with headline/5 items/mini recipe/WhatsApp button/share-card button → favorite persists → Saved tab lists the item (saved-item-6a6685855a9bce39114e7999). One minor console deprecation warning surfaced: `props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents` originating from the off-screen `<View style={styles.offscreen} pointerEvents="none">` at /app/frontend/app/pairing/[id].tsx:202 — non-blocking but should be migrated to `style.pointerEvents` for consistency with the toast.tsx fix. Also observed a benign `useNativeDriver` web warning (expected on web preview).

react_native_issues.issue: Uses deprecated `pointerEvents` prop instead of `style.pointerEvents`. Warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Reference: /app/frontend/app/pairing/[id].tsx:202 — change `<View style={styles.offscreen} pointerEvents="none">` to include `pointerEvents: 'none'` inside the style object (same pattern used in src/components/toast.tsx).

action_items: Migrate `pointerEvents="none"` prop on the off-screen PairingShareCard wrapper (pairing/[id].tsx line 202) into the style object to silence the React Native Web deprecation warning.
critical_code_review_comments: Off-screen render pattern (position: absolute, left: -9999, opacity: 0) works and does not add scroll space, but on real devices consider `collapsable={false}` already applied inside PairingShareCard — good. Ensure captureRef is invoked only after the card has mounted (currently guaranteed because the button lives in the same ScrollView).
shareCard() correctly early-returns on Platform.OS === 'web' before touching captureRef, so react-native-view-shot is never called on web — verified: no console error triggered on tap.
